title: Outlook: Cloud Policy controls for Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows
summary: The briefing distinguishes the planned Outlook controls from existing Cloud Policy and Exchange mailbox policies, and its roadmap facts and documented settings are supported. The Cloud Policy wizard path needs one minor completion for selecting the target groups; the Exchange navigation flagged by the pre-check is confirmed by another cited Microsoft page.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy can enforce Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise policy settings on a user's device even if it is not domain joined or otherwise managed.
claims.quote: Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365 lets you enforce policy settings for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise on a user's device, even if the device isn't domain joined or otherwise managed.

claims.claim: Some Cloud Policy settings can already be enforced for Office for the web.
claims.quote: You can also enforce some policy settings for Office for the web and Loop, both for guests who are signed in and for users who access documents anonymously.

claims.claim: Learn says most existing Cloud Policy settings for Outlook apply only to classic Outlook.
claims.quote: All ADMX policies and most policies from Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365 (Cloud policies) apply only to classic Outlook.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Most new Outlook features can currently be managed through Exchange policies rather than Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: You can manage most features with Exchange PowerShell cmdlets. However, for features that span multiple Microsoft 365 experiences, like Loop and in-product Feedback, as well as settings for Diagnostic Data and Connected Experiences, you should use Cloud Policy.

claims.claim: Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -SignaturesEnabled $false is an Exchange PowerShell operation that prevents Outlook on the web users from manually creating signatures.
claims.quote: Admins can use either of the following methods to prevent Outlook on the web users from manually creating email signatures: Exchange PowerShell: Use the SignaturesEnabled parameter with the value $false on the Set-OwaMailboxPolicy cmdlet.

claims.claim: Most mailbox policies apply to both Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows and cannot be enabled for only one of those clients.
claims.quote: Most of the mailbox policies apply to both Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, so you can't enable them on one client but not the other.
